newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bars magazine over "undesirable" sex ads.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bars magazine over "undesirable" sex ads.

text.p: The Singapore government has not renewed the publication licence of IS Magazine due to objections to lewd advertisements in the fortnightly, a spokesman for the Ministry of Information and the Arts (MITA) said on Tuesday.
The spokesman said IS Magazine flouted publishing guidelines issued by MITA by printing objectionable items.
These included telephone numbers offering phone sex, ads which are lewd and ads which promote undesirable lifestyles, it said.

"Despite receiving more than one warning from MITA, IS Magazine continued to carry ads encouraging homosexuality in their recent issues," the spokesman said in a written reply to queries from Reuters.
"As they have not heeded our warnings, MITA has decided not to renew their permit."
The magazine's licence expired on June 12.
Earlier on Tuesday, the magazine's publisher and editor-in-chief said MITA had objections to its personal advertisement section.
"A licence the first time was not renewed but we have re-applied on the 16th of June," Gretchen Worth told Reuters.
IS Magazine is a free fortnightly which covers lifestyle and entertainment and has been in circulation here about two years.
Worth said that along with the new application for renewal of its licence, it had removed the personals pages.
"Our feeling is that removing the personals page does actually take care of the objections that were raised to us, regarding why MITA did not renew the permit," Worth said.
She declined to comment on the nature of the advertisements.
MITA confirmed the magazine had written to appeal against the action and that this was under consideration.

Singapore practices censorship and imposes restrictions on the media in various areas to protect what it views as basic values, and does not subscribe to liberal Western concepts of a free press. A number of foreign magazines, including Playboy, Penthouse and Cosmopolitan, are not allowed to circulate in the city state.

In 1989, MITA revoked the permit issued to Artistic Monthly, a Chinese entertainment tabloid, for carrying nude pictures reproduced from banned publications. The publisher did not appeal against the decision.
In the current case, MITA noted it had not revoked IS Magazine's permit. The licence was merely not renewed upon expiry.
IS magazine is published by Hong Kong-based company Asia City Publishing Group and has an audited circulation of 25,000.
